blocks.text: Egyptians are famous in the Arab world for their humor: the ready joke (il-ʾafša), the self-irony, the play of words, the proverb quoted at the right time. Understanding humor is one of the last steps to truly understand a language, and also one of the most useful: in conversations, shows, social media and even talk shows, irony is everywhere. In this unity learn the vocabulary of humor (dammu ḫafīf, nukta, ʾafša), a choice of very used proverbs and frequent idiomatic expressions (fi l-mišmiš, kalām fi l-hawa, ʾalbi ʾayilli), the way to react to a joke and some rules about when and with whom to joke. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-10, B2-11 and B2-12.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 193–201), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, comedy and Egyptian humorous videos (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. understanding and using the vocabulary of humor (dammu ḫafīf / tʾīl, nukta, ʾafša, biyitrayyaʾ);
2. recognize and use a dozen frequent Egyptian proverbs, with their sense;
3. understanding and using common idiomatic expressions of conversation;
4. react to a joke and respond to a friendly mockery;
5. to understand when humor is suitable and when not.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

blocks.text: The ʾafša. It is the exchange of quick lines, an Egyptian tradition: one throws an ironic phrase, the other immediately responds with another, playing on words. It is not a matter of offending but of showing readiness: those who remain unanswered laugh first.

blocks.text: Use a proverb. An Egyptian proverb is not quoted as a curiosity: it fits into the conversation to close a speech, advise, console. After a proverb, you often add zayy but biyʾūlu As it is said to be: biyʾūl... the proverb says... The lentil proverb (illi) ma-yiʿrafš yiʾūl ʿads) is the analyst's proverb: those who do not know complete history judge badly. It's said to whom he's drawing hasty conclusions.

chapters.title: 8. When to joke and listen to authentic humor

blocks.text: The unwritten rules. With friends, humor is continuous, even pungent. With older people or people you don't know, wait till they're the first to joke. You are happy to joke about yourself, about traffic, about heat, about football; avoid joking about religion, the family of others and political issues with those you don't know. A joke that offends someone is not hazār: è tarʾīʾa. What to listen to. Egyptian comedies (films and series), sketches and comic monologues, humorous social videos. Many jokes play on two-way words or references to famous films: don't worry about understanding them all. See Appendix C. The method for a comedy scene.
